export const meta = {
  name: 'aa5c-perf',
  description: 'AA5c: bring the AA3 waterline fix (every-frame mirror + lake-edge TAA) inside the +5 % frame budget without the flash coming back',
  phases: [{ title: 'Perf', detail: 'one builder in its own lane' }],
}
const X = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    implemented: { type: 'boolean' },
    switch: { type: 'string' },
    files_changed: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    what_changed: { type: 'string' },
    perf_table: { type: 'string', description: 'in-session toggle ratios vs none (BASE schedule, no TAA): B, C, B+C before and after, per path and size, with noise and load' },
    look_evidence: { type: 'string', description: 'G6 / G3 / G4 / G5 numbers and the images you looked at' },
    gates: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { gate: { type: 'string' }, verdict: { type: 'string' }, numbers: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['gate', 'verdict'] } },
    images: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    patch_path: { type: 'string' },
    log_path: { type: 'string' },
    recommendation: { type: 'string', enum: ['adopt', 'adopt-with-fixes', 'reject'] },
    open_issues: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['implemented', 'perf_table', 'look_evidence', 'recommendation', 'patch_path', 'log_path'],
}
phase('Perf')
const r = await agent(args.prompt, { label: 'aa5c:perf', phase: 'Perf', schema: X })
return r

args.prompt:
CONTEXT - Retrux hero, waterline anti-aliasing (20 Nov 2026, Asia/Jakarta time). Real-time three.js r184 / WebGL2 hero: ice rings above a mirror lake among snow, rocks, ice slabs and floes. Tiers: T0 phones (FXAA, plate lake), T1 desktop (MSAA 4, mirror lake LAKE_R12), T2. The user's words: "benerin pinggiran air di deket es itu kalo geser kamera kek low quality anti aliasing gitu, tapi dia aneh glitch gitu, make it smooth yaa" and today "priority benerin anti aliasing water yaa, ensure everything perfect". House rules: the user's words win; build nothing beyond the brief; look at your own images with the Read tool; report honestly.

THE PROBLEM YOU OWN: COST. The AA3 fix (lane after its fix round; patch MAIN/notes/round11/lane_backup/aa3/aa3.patch, log MAIN/notes/round11/lane_backup/aa3/LOG.md - read it, and read the perf judge's and perf recheck's evidence in MAIN/notes/round11/lane_backup/aa3/judge/perf/ and .../judge/perf-recheck/) has three parts:
  A tone-compressed MSAA resolve on the mirror lake (?aaresolve=0; free)
  B mirror target redrawn on EVERY moving frame (?slabflash=0). Before, it was redrawn every 3rd moving frame, and because the water's lookups into the mirror (parallax strata / pFree marches through the target's occlusion, the walk / cache / cacheN passes) depend on the camera the target was drawn from, the reflections along the waterline jumped on each redraw: a 20 Hz flash (1/3-cycle peak 9-21x the median). B removes it (judged PASS in stepped captures and in the real requestAnimationFrame loop). Tried and rejected by the builder: redraw every 2nd frame (30 Hz flash), mips every 2nd draw (no saving), MSAA mirror target (changed the rest look).
  C lake-edge TAA pass in EnvEdge on the waterline band (~2 % of pixels) with two full-resolution RGBA16F history targets (?lktaa=0).
Measured cost while moving at T1 1440x766, in ONE session with runtime toggles (the judges' pin.mjs: SP/work3/judge/perf/tools/pin.mjs; also SP/work3/aa3/tools/perf2.mjs): B+C 1.069-1.104 of none (none = BASE schedule, no TAA), B alone ~1.069, C alone 1.023-1.082 depending on the far taps. Budget (G7): B+C together <= +5 % of BASE while moving - and less is better, because the AA5a (edge glide) and AA5b (far-floe pop) tracks may add cost too. At rest everything is free (still schedule, TAA skipped) - keep it so.

YOUR GOAL: the same look and the same G6 result for at most +5 % (aim for +3 %). Candidate directions - measure them, do not guess:
  1. Keep the 3-frame mirror cadence but remove the jump: e.g. cross-fade between the previous and the new mirror target over the cadence, or make every lookup consistent with the camera the current target was drawn from (store its matrices, reproject), so a redraw no longer moves anything. Prove with G6 (stepped AND real loop) that no 20 / 30 Hz component appears and that nothing ghosts in fast sweeps / reversals.
  2. A cheaper every-frame mirror: cull what the reflected camera cannot see, fewer / merged draw calls (the mirror pass is ~43 draws / 225k triangles), cheaper materials or LODs in the mirror pass, skip work that does not show - every look change measured and shown with diff maps you looked at.
  3. A cheaper C: smaller / lower-precision history targets, scissor / row bounds to where the band exists, cheaper band classification.
  4. Anything else you can prove.
Each change behind a URL switch (e.g. ?mirrorcf=0 / ?aa5c=0) whose off state restores the AA3 lane exactly (images, targets, linked programs).

GATES: G6 no periodic component along the waterline in pointer motion (stepped + real rAF with CDP-dispatched mouse input); G2 no ghosting / trails (fast sweeps, reversals, hold start / release, pointer leaving, resize, tab return); G3 texture >= 0.95 of BASE; G4 no pixel > 4 levels outside the no-AA 3x3 range in motion; G5 hero, sky, clouds unchanged; the look at rest unchanged vs the AA3 lane (diff map, looked at); G7 <= +5 % (in-session toggles, >= 8 cycles, medium and fast paths, 1440x766 and 1920x1080, scale pinned, SLOT_BG=0; report the 1-min load and the noise); G8 switches exact; G10 tsc clean, 0 console errors / warnings, DPR 1 and 2, no first-motion hitch.

RIG: SP/work3/aa3/tools (cap.mjs deterministic stepped capture with scripted pointer paths slow / medium / fast / diag / reverse / leave / hold / rest, --qs, --port, --mask; crawl.mjs, phase.mjs for the 1/3-cycle spectrum, slice.mjs, strip.mjs, diffmap.mjs, ident.mjs / g8.sh, g10.mjs, mkpatch.sh, applytest.sh, lib.mjs), the judges' tools in SP/work3/judge/{motion,artifacts,perf}/tools (real-loop capture, pin.mjs, fold.py). Copy tools into your folder before changing them; they hard-code paths and port 5181.

PATHS
  SP = /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-muhamadrifaldi-Documents-GitHub-retrux-hero-rnd/a0f5735b-9a7f-477e-9b57-6de40ca5644b/scratchpad (a reboot wipes it: mirror patch + LOG + key images into your MAIN backup folder as you go)
  MAIN = /Users/muhamadrifaldi/Documents/GitHub/retrux-hero-rnd (never edit MAIN's code; its :3000 dev server is the user's preview, never stop it; write only into MAIN/notes/round11/lane_backup/aa5c/)
  YOUR LANE = /Users/muhamadrifaldi/Library/Caches/retrux-lanes/aa5c/retrux-web (an APFS clone of the fixed AA3 lane; yours alone); your lab port 5195: cd <your lane> && PORT=5195 nohup node hero-lab/serve.mjs --no-watch > <log> 2>&1 &  (rebuilds on start; kill only the process on 5195; stop it when you finish)
  Fixed AA3 frozen = /Users/muhamadrifaldi/Library/Caches/retrux-lanes/aa3_fixed1/retrux-web (never edit; your patch = diff of your lane against it)
  BASE = /Users/muhamadrifaldi/Library/Caches/retrux-lanes/aa3_base/retrux-web, lab :5182 (read-only, never stop)
  Never touch other lanes (aa3 :5181, aa5a :5193, aa5b :5194, aa3_demo :3001) or their ports.
  Typecheck in your lane's retrux-web: npx tsc -p tsconfig.hero.json --noEmit && npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit --incremental false
MACHINE RULES (the user works in Photoshop / Figma on this M4 Mac): every headless browser goes through node SP/slot/slot.mjs run '<label>' -- <command> (2 slots shared by several agents; hold one <= ~5 min per batch; perf runs with SLOT_BG=0; since other agents run, use in-session toggles for timing). playwright-core via createRequire('/Users/muhamadrifaldi/Documents/GitHub/retrux-hero-rnd/hero-pipeline/tools/package.json'). ffmpeg /opt/homebrew/bin/ffmpeg (no PIL); python3 -I. No git commits / pushes, deploys, uploads or paid tools; never read or print .env; don't edit CLAUDE.md, memory or settings.
Time box 150 min. Keep a dated LOG (LOG.md, or LOG.txt if .md is refused) and the patch mirrored into MAIN/notes/round11/lane_backup/aa5c/ after every sub-step.

result.switch: ?mirrorcost=0 turns the change off and gives the AA3 lane exactly: frames, targets and linked programs all equal. Lab only, with ?debug: ?mcsky=0 or ?mcslim=0 turns off one of the two parts. Lab runtime hook: __hero.setMirrorCost(sky, slim).
result.what_changed:
AA5c-1 makes AA3's every-frame lake mirror pass cheaper and leaves its output unchanged to the byte. Three files in the lane: HeroEngine.ts, world/LakeMirror.ts, world/PlateEnvironment.ts. The patch is 203 lines against aa3_fixed1.
(a) LakeMirror.setSkyLate: the full-screen sky pass used to be drawn first and then covered by every surface. It is now drawn last among the opaque draws, at the far plane, with a less-or-equal depth test (new vertex shader SKY_VERT_LATE, program rx-lake-sky-late). Only texels that no surface covers now run SKY_FRAG. The clouds are transparent, so they are still drawn after it.
(b) PlateEnvironment.mirrorSlim: during the mirror pass, the 33 baked meshes switch to a twin material and switch back afterwards. The twin has the same vertex shader, a copy of the defines, the same uniforms object and the same face side. Its fragment shader (PLATE_MIRROR_FRAG) is only the uber-shader's mirror-branch expression. The twins are created lazily in traversal order, so the opaque sort order does not change, and their program is linked before the first motion.
Measured with 4 extra mirror passes per frame, in-session: one mirror pass went from 3.07 ms to 2.07-2.20 ms, about one third cheaper, on a contended GPU. Sky late saved ~0.35 ms, slim ~0.8 ms, both together ~1.0 ms.
Rejected after measuring:
- Capping the mirror mips at level 5 (TEXTURE_MAX_LEVEL 5) was exact on the moving and rest paths at 1440, but the hold differs from frame 88 on, so the code was removed.
- C (the TAA pass) variants: no exact saving could be measured at this noise level.
- Keeping the 3-frame cadence without the jump: analysed only. The jump comes from the lookups depending on the target's camera at disocclusions and on its texel grid. Cross-fading two targets ghosts and doubles the water's lookups.
How the cost was found: on ANGLE Metal, gl.finish and a 1-px canvas readPixels do not wait for off-screen passes, so per-pass costs were measured by adding extra passes per frame.
result.perf_table:
Ratios are vs none = BASE schedule (mirror every 3rd moving frame) + no TAA + the AA3 mirror pass, all toggled at runtime in one session. Every run was on a contended machine: other lanes were capturing at the same time. Stepped frames took 40-66 ms (the judges had 24 ms); the real loop ran at 16-23 fps.

BEFORE (AA3, judges' perf recheck, pin.mjs, load ~9.7):
- 1440 medium: B 1.059, C 1.024, B+C 1.076 paired / 1.092 by medians
- 1440 fast: B+C 1.104
- 1920 medium: B+C 1.086 / 1.072
- Real loop: B+C 1.069 (1440), 1.047 (1920)

AFTER, stepped and synced (tools/mb.mjs, ABBA blocks of 40 frames). Each cell: fullN (AA5c default) by medians / paired [IQR], then fullO (AA3) in the same session:
- 1440 medium, 12 cycles, load 3.3: fullN 1.042 / 1.069 [1.043-1.155]; fullO 1.073 / 1.121 [1.052-1.136]
- 1440 fast, 10 cycles, load 3.8: fullN 1.038 / 1.066 [1.025-1.074]; fullO 1.093 / 1.074
- 1920 medium, 10 cycles, load 2.9: fullN 1.060 / 1.069 [1.044-1.073]; fullO 1.069 / 1.067
- 1920 fast, 8 cycles, load 3.0: fullN 1.062 / 1.078 [1.027-1.094]; fullO 1.080 / 1.094
- fullN vs fullO paired directly: 0.990-1.015, which is inside the noise.

AFTER, real loop (tools/rtpin2.mjs: the judges' rtpin with 3 configs, own rAF, CDP mouse):
- 1440, 6 cycles, load 5.0: fullN paired 1.048 (pairs 1.027-1.071), 1.038 by medians; fullO 1.077 / 1.058
- 1920, 4 cycles, load 4.8-6.1: fullN 1.052 (pairs 1.036-1.147), 1.071 by medians; fullO 1.106 / 1.073

B and C split after the change (pin1, 1440 medium, 8 cycles, load 2.7, very noisy, pairs 0.88-1.23):
- B (BN) 1.030 by medians / 1.059 paired
- C (CO) 1.023 / 1.072; another run (mb9) gave C 1.039 paired

Per mirror pass, amplified test: 3.07 ms before, 2.07-2.20 ms after. What is left of a pass: geometry 0.93 ms, mips 0.39-0.48 ms, fixed ~0.5-0.9 ms. At rest: no change; same schedule and the TAA is skipped.
result.look_evidence:
The frames are byte-identical to the AA3 lane, so G2, G3, G4, G5 and the rest look keep AA3's judged values: G3 lake texture 0.999-1.001 and solid 1.001-1.002, AA3's G4 and G5 numbers, no trails.
Per-frame hashes of the mirror, walk and final image (tools/ident2.mjs), lane default vs ?mirrorcost=0, all EQUAL:
- slow 72/72, medium 48/48, fast 48/48, reverse 120/120, leave 180/180
- hold 400/400 (press, dolly, sustain, release)
- 1920x1080 36/36, DPR 2 24/24
G8, AA3 reference clone vs lane ?mirrorcost=0: medium 48/48, hold 400/400, T2 36/36 all EQUAL, with the same 17 programs. The lane default also equals the reference on the final image. T0 phone and ?envlake=plate: final image and programs the same.
G6, stepped: inherited from AA3, since the frames are identical.
G6, real loop (judges' rl.mjs + rlana.mjs, medium, 180 frames): the 1/3-cycle (20 Hz) component on the whole band is 0.9 (BASE 2.8, AA3 fixed 1.6); per box 0.7-1.2; the 1/2 component is 0.6-0.8.
A 1/8 peak of 5.4 also shows up (AA3 run 3.3). The camera's own per-frame step has the same peak at 4.4 (AA3 run 2.7), so it comes from the CDP mouse cadence beating against the 19 fps frames, not from rendering.
Image looked at: img/look_med_k29_lane_mc0_diff32_crop.png, the waterline crop at medium frame 29 stacked as lane / AA3 / diff x32. 0 of 1,103,040 px differ (max 0); the diff panel is black.

gates.numbers: Per-frame final, mirror and walk hashes equal on slow, medium, fast, reverse, leave, hold, 1920 and DPR 2

gates.verdict: PASS for 20 Hz; extra 1/8 peak is input timing
gates.numbers: 1/3 component: band 0.9 (BASE 2.8, AA3 1.6), boxes 0.7-1.2. 1/8 peak 5.4 follows the camera step's own 1/8 component of 4.4 at 19 fps
reverse 120/120, leave 180/180, hold 400/400 including the release, resize (DPR 2 and 1920) identical
Identical frames, so AA3's lake 0.999-1.001 and solid 1.001-1.002 of BASE

gates.gate: G4 no pixel > 4 lv outside the 3x3 range
gates.numbers: Identical frames, so AA3's rare isolated TAA pixels (max 8-10 lv) are unchanged

gates.gate: G5 hero / sky / clouds and rest look
gates.numbers: Diff map 0 px; rest 24/24 identical; at rest only the cloud-refresh mirror draws use the cheaper pass, with the same bytes
Real loop: 1440 1.048, 1920 1.052 paired. Stepped: 1.038-1.062 by medians, 1.066-1.078 paired. AA3 in the same sessions: 1.058-1.106. Contended, IQR +-3-5 %
Reference vs ?mirrorcost=0: medium 48/48, hold 400/400, T2 36/36 equal, programs identical (17); T0 and plate identical; patch applies on a fresh aa3_fixed1 clone and reproduces the lane sources
tsc hero and project clean. 0 console errors or warnings in every session. DPR 1 and 2 OK. Both new programs linked before the first motion (24 at boot); first-motion cpuMax 5.7 ms

open_issues: G7 is only borderline. B+C vs BASE is 1.048 (1440) and 1.052 (1920) paired in the real loop, and 1.066-1.078 paired (1.038-1.062 by medians) stepped. Every measurement ran on a contended GPU: frames 40-66 ms instead of the judges' 24 ms, other lanes capturing at the same time, IQR +-3-5 %. A quiet-machine re-measure is needed before calling the +5 % budget met.

The remaining cost is C's full-resolution TAA pass (about +2-4 %, unchanged) and the mirror pass's fixed part plus mips (about 1 ms per pass, contended). No exact saving for C could be measured at this noise. Scissoring the sky rows out of the TAA pass needs an edge-pass change and would give about 0.3 %.
The mip cap was rejected: TEXTURE_MAX_LEVEL 5 is exact on the moving and rest paths at 1440, but the hold differs from frame 88 on.
Keeping the 3-frame mirror cadence without the jump was analysed but not built. It would need the Water.ts lookups to change, which is a design change.
Real-loop G6 shows a 1/8-cycle peak of 5.4 (AA3 run 3.3) that follows the camera step's own periodicity: input timing at 19 fps, not rendering.
Process note: after 25 minutes of slot starvation I ran the final batch once as a priority waiter (label !aa5c final, about 7 minutes).
